correctness.rationale: Subtract c/(1-s) and stack all L+1 history layers. The steady state is admissible and unique by the maximum-norm s-contraction on time-constant vectors. At the unique positive root (the product decreases strictly from infinity to s^n), the cycle equations v_i=s H_i(r)v_{i-1} close consistently with v_i>0. The layer values r^{-k}v_i give a strictly positive eigenvector of the actual lifted matrix, including zero lag weights or unused layers. Similarity by the diagonal of this vector produces a nonnegative matrix with row sums r, so the induced infinity norm and spectral radius are both r; a small positive multiple of the eigenvector realizes equality from an admissible history. This checks the worst-case quantifier without assuming primitivity, or a rate for each initial history. At fixed r<1, Jensen gives H_i(r)≥r^{-(1+μ_i)}, with equality only for a deterministic law; monotonicity moves the unit root strictly to the right if any lag law is mixed. Every feasible integer total can be distributed among the bounded integer lags. With fixed individual means, extend the strictly convex lag values by piecewise linear interpolation to obtain the adjacent-integer minimum; the endpoint chord gives the maximum. Strictness on other discrete supports forces the extremizers, with the trivial singleton and two-point degeneracies included. Likewise a strict convex-order change increases the transform: on a finite integer support the discrete second differences of r^{-k} are positive and at least one call expectation changes. The example independently reduces to 8r^5−3r^4−1=0 with root 0.75655233305921373596…, versus 1/√2 for both fixed budgets. This is deterministic weighting of histories, not a stochastic switching model.
